blocks.text: This is an invented record for a comparison prototype Q version 0, not a claim about your P1 runs. Q ignores the quiet condition when searching. Its trace explains the R4 failure. In the same fictional comparison, the manual baseline produced the expected result and correct explanation on all four cases: 4 of 4 full passes. Q achieved 3 of 4. The denominator includes the failed case.

On this set Q has fewer full passes than the baseline. This supports investigating its quiet check; it does not establish performance on all requests. Do not claim a speed advantage because we did not measure time. Correct implementations of P1 and the baseline can both pass all four, in which case these results show no correctness advantage for either method.

guided_practice.title: Run a fair comparison
guided_practice.prompt: Operate your saved P1 cards and the manual baseline on all four R cases. Record actual results and traces on your sheet. Summarise full passes over all attempted cases for each method, name any failures and explain why a tie would not prove the prototype improves correctness. Do not invent an observed run.
guided_practice.answer: A correctly executed P1 and baseline both produce B1, B2, no match, no match with correct reasons, giving 4 of 4 each. Accept an honest record of different observed results when the pupil identifies and investigates the disagreements. Both methods must use the same requests, catalogue and pass criterion. A tie establishes no correctness advantage on this set; an unperformed run must remain unperformed.

independent_case.title: Audit a new test record
independent_case.task: Independently audit this fictional equipment selector. Catalogue E has E1 first with capacity 4 and E2 second with capacity 8. Valid group sizes are whole numbers 1 to 10. Select the first item with capacity at least the group size, or no match; invalid input needs clarification. The saved prototype reports E1 for group 3 with reason “4 holds 3”; E1 for group 6 with reason “4 holds 6”; no match for group 9 with reason “both too small”. Write all expected results, mark full passes, calculate the fraction and explain the failure. Give one untested input category. No booking occurs.
independent_case.answer: Expected group 3: E1 because 4 holds 3. Group 6: E2 because E1 is too small and 8 holds 6. Group 9: no match because both capacities are too small. The first and third pass; the second fails both output and reason, giving 2 of 3 full passes. The record suggests a capacity-check problem but the saved instructions and trace are needed to locate it. Missing, nonwhole or out-of-range input is untested, as is equality with a capacity.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: A correct label is always a full pass
The agreed criterion also requires a correct explanation.
Remove a failed run because something went wrong
Keep and investigate it; missing required output cannot count as success.
Four passes prove all inputs work
The conclusion is limited by the selected cases and conditions.
The prototype must beat the manual baseline
A correct simple baseline can tie or outperform a prototype; report the evidence.

PROCESS  run unchanged prototype and observe
OUTPUT  actual result, pass/fail, and notes
CORE IDEA  Repeated success on ordinary cases is necessary but not sufficient.

UNDER THE HOOD  A test case includes input, setup, expected behavior, actual behavior, and result. Precommitting expectations reduces hindsight bias. Repeated normal tests establish basic reliability but say little about uncommon conditions.
Draw a fresh example with all three stages:
A closer explanation

blocks.title: From a planned case to evidence
blocks.caption: Keep the catalogue, requests and pass criteria the same for the prototype and baseline.

blocks.text: Give each case an ID. Record its exact input, purpose, expected output and expected explanation before running it. Then add observed output, observed explanation, pass or fail, and a trace reference. Put the prototype version, catalogue version and baseline method at the top of the sheet. A pass needs the correct result and a reason supported by the checked conditions; the right activity with a false reason is not a full pass.

Our routine set R contains four valid requests. R1 is 11 minutes Yes, checking an early quiet match. R2 is 9 minutes No, checking that the search reaches a later fitting row. R3 is 6 minutes No, checking that a valid request can exhaust the list. R4 is 9 minutes Yes, checking that a time fit alone is insufficient. These cases do not cover every accepted input or validation error.
